_readme.purpose: Standing catalyst calendar. Holds dated events the earnings API does NOT provide: investor/analyst days, conferences, product launches, sales/delivery reports, FDA action dates, splits, shareholder meetings, filing deadlines, and macro speaking events. Routine earnings are pulled live from the earnings calendar and do not belong here.
consumed_by: daily premarket report - today's entries feed the game plan, next 5 days feed the This Week EVENTS column
Sunday week-ahead page - full following-week view
rules: time is 12-hour Central Time, or null when only the date is known
verified=true requires a real source URL; verified=false renders as tentative, never as fact
never add an entry without a source - omit it instead
Significance to the ticker is the bar, not event category. No filing deadlines, no routine conference appearances, no filler. If it cannot move the name, it does not go in.

Scope is the universe list plus market-wide macro. Do NOT add off-universe tickers just because they crossed a newsletter - if an off-universe name has a genuinely huge catalyst, add it deliberately and say why.

AMENDED 2026-08-17: market cap earns consideration on its own. A large-cap off-universe name gets evaluated on merit rather than auto-rejected for not being on the list. Pull the real cap before judging - do not eyeball it. Cap alone is not sufficient though: weigh it against event-type signal, where monthly sales/results releases and analyst days are high signal, plain conference appearances are low, and annual shareholder MEETINGS are near-zero regardless of cap.
Entries with no announced date use date:null plus a date_window string. Never assign a placeholder date to an undated event.
_readme.fields: ticker | name | type | date (YYYY-MM-DD) | time_ct | note | source | verified

events.name: Apple
events.note: CEO TRANSITION TAKES EFFECT. John Ternus, SVP of Hardware Engineering, becomes CEO; Tim Cook becomes executive chairman of the board; Arthur Levinson, non-executive chairman for the past 15 years, becomes lead independent director. Announced April 2026 and unanimously approved by the board, so the news is old but THE EFFECTIVE DATE IS 9/1 - this is Apple's first CEO transition since Cook succeeded Jobs in 2011. recurring_patterns.COST: Monthly sales report, released AFTER THE CLOSE, in the first week or so of the following month. Confirmed pattern from Costco IR: Sept 2025 sales reported Oct 8; Oct 2025 sales reported Nov 5. So Aug 2026 sales land early Sept, Sept 2026 sales land early Oct. Exact dates are not pre-announced far ahead - check investor.costco.com in the final week of each month.

coverage._why: Holds the RECORD of forward sweeps. checked_through is derived from coverage.sweeps by catalyst_sweep.coverage_through() and must never be hand-set: on 2026-09-13 the week-ahead published "no verified slate exists for this week" while OSCR's Investor Day and Salesforce's Dreamforce investor session were both scheduled for 9/16. The file had simply stopped being swept - git shows exactly one forward sweep ever, on 2026-08-13 - and an empty query result was indistinguishable from nobody having looked.

sweeps.method: Category sweep 2026-09-13 for 9/13-10/13. Searched: investor/analyst day announcements for Oct 2026; Tesla Q3 delivery cadence + GM/Ford/Rivian Q3 sales; NVIDIA GTC and AMD/Meta/Amazon product events; Snapdragon Summit and Adobe MAX; plus the broker high-market-cap earnings calendar across the full 30 days. LIMITS - this was a CATEGORY sweep, not 51 individual IR pages. Off-universe hits deliberately excluded: WDAY analyst day 10/13, CLS 10/27, BWXT 9/29. Outside horizon: NVDA GTC Washington Nov 30-Dec 3. UNRESOLVED: Adobe MAX dates conflict between the official site (Nov 10-12, Miami Beach) and secondary sources (Oct 28-30, LA) - outside this horizon either way, must be settled before the horizon reaches late October. NVDA GTC Berlin is an October regional event with no date found.

CORRECTIVE sweep 2026-09-14 over the SAME 9/13-10/13 window already recorded as swept. The 9/13 category sweep was searched via general web queries and MISSED all six of these, including two tier-one macro releases (August Retail Sales the morning of the decision, Bank of England the next day) and INTU's investor day - a name that sits in our own investor-day study. They were caught only because Marcus supplied the weekly Catalyst Watch newsletter plus an events-calendar screenshot. LESSON: general web search is NOT an adequate sweep instrument. It surfaces what was PRESS-RELEASED and misses the scheduled calendar - macro releases, conference slates, regulatory hearings, and the long tail of investor days. The weekly catalyst newsletter and a real events calendar are the primary instruments; web search is only for confirming a specific event against company IR.
